subject: Clarify: Cross-border usage credits & tiered per-token discounts
body:
Message 1 (2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00)
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@datawave.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Subject: Clarify hosted API discounts for multi-region usage

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the low latency on the EU nodes was impressive. Procurement asked me to get clarity on how Redwood applies per-token volume discounts when usage spans multiple regions. Our traffic is ~60% US, 30% EU (data residency required), 10% APAC, and we expect bursty spikes into APAC during marketing events.

Questions we need answered to move forward: 
- Do commits/tiers apply globally or are tokens bucketed by billing region?
- If tokens are bucketed, how are discounts applied when we exceed a tier in one region but not others?
- Can we get a blended rate or a credit for cross-border failover (we plan to fail over to US when EU is down but want that traffic priced fairly)?
- Any options for temporary APAC burst protection without committing to long-term APAC spend?

Procurement would like a short written summary we can attach to our SOW and a MAP (mutual action plan) that lists next steps and timelines. Can you also point me to the legal/finance contact who handles regional tax or VAT questions?

Appreciate it — aiming to finalize vendor shortlist next week.

Best,
Sofia Alvarez
Head of ML Products
DataWave

----

Message 2 (2026-11-08T11:03:00-08:00)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@datawave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API discounts for multi-region usage

Hi Sofia — great to connect. Short answers up front, then a proposed path: 

High level:
- Commits are flexible: we can model commits either as a single global pool or as region-specific buckets. Global pools simplify discounts (one blended tier based on total committed tokens), region buckets give you stronger guarantees / isolation for residency and SLA.
- If you choose region buckets, discounts apply per-bucket; we support dynamic rebalancing credits so if one region underruns while another overruns, we can apply transfer credits during the contract year (subject to cap).
- For cross-border failover, we offer a failover credit: up to X% of monthly committed tokens can be billed at the originating region's blended rate instead of the failover region surcharge. We usually configure this in the MAP.
- For temporary APAC bursts, we can add a non-recurring burst buffer (30–90 day window) at a discounted rate vs. on-demand; or a small reserved APAC bucket you can scale out of.

What I will attach: a draft pricing proposal (pricing_proposal_v2.pdf) with two pathways (Global Pool vs Region Buckets) and a MAP spreadsheet (MAP.xlsx) with timelines and approval owners.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the proposal + MAP (attached).
2) You and procurement pick preferred pathway (global pool or buckets) and mark tolerances for failover credits.
3) We’ll run a brief pricing model with your historical split to show blended vs bucketed costs.
4) Finance/legal from both sides get on a call for VAT/tax and SOW language.

Who should I loop from your finance team? I’ll also loop Ben from pricing and Marcus from strategic accounts to finalize concession ranges.

Thanks — attaching docs now.

—
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: pricing_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal), MAP.xlsx (mutual action plan)

----

Message 3 (2026-11-09T08:27:00-08:00)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Subject: Fwd: Clarify hosted API discounts for multi-region usage

Kim / Marcus — forwarding the DataWave thread. Key items for negotiation:
- They prefer a single invoice / simplified economics for procurement but need EU residency guarantees. We can offer a Global Pool with a carve-out contract clause that guarantees data residency for EU traffic (audit logs + dedicated EU model endpoints) while counting tokens toward the global pool. That gets them simplified billing and us a single commit.
- Fallback credit: propose 20% of committed monthly tokens eligible for failover credit at originating-region rate for first 12 months. After that, scale back to 5% unless they add APAC commit.
- Discount bands: current price band table (for hosted API) is 0–100M, 100M–500M, 500M+ tokens. Consider deepening the middle band for this enterprise (e.g., 12% -> 15%) if they sign a 12-month commit and 18% for 24-month.
- APAC burst buffer: propose a 90-day trial reserve (non-recurring) at 60% of the standard on-demand surcharge.

Questions for Marcus: do we have precedent for Global Pool + residency carve-out (legal okay with that)? Also what's the max concession we can approve without EVP sign-off (sales comp and margin constraints)?

—Ben
Director, Strategic Pricing

----

Message 4 (2026-11-10T17:46:00-08:00)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@datawave.ai>, DataWave Procurement <procurement@datawave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Clarify hosted API discounts for multi-region usage — proposal and MAP

Sofia — attaching the formal proposal and a filled MAP. Highlights inside the doc:
- Option A (Global Pool): single committed token pool, blended discount tiers based on total commit. Includes an EU residency carve-out: dedicated EU endpoints and contract clause guaranteeing EU origin processing with audit logs.
- Option B (Region Buckets): separate commit per region; stronger SLAs in each region and potentially higher effective discounts per-region if volumes support it.
- Failover credit: 20% of committed tokens eligible for originating-region billing rate for 12 months; after 12 months we can renegotiate or require APAC commit if APAC usage remains >15% monthly.
- APAC burst buffer: one 90-day trial reserve at a reduced surcharge, automatically expires.
- Suggested discount bands for DataWave: 12-month term -> 15% middle band, 24-month -> 18% middle band.

I included a short pricing model tab where we plugged in the split you shared (60/30/10) — in your case the Global Pool gives a small blended saving vs strictly bucketed approach unless APAC growth accelerates.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm preferred Option (Global Pool vs Region Buckets) and whether procurement wants the failover credit at 20% or to request a different % by Tue (2026-11-17).
2) Share the name and email of your finance/tax reviewer; we’ll set a 30-minute cadence call to close SOW language.
3) If you want a firm quote, sign the attached MAP and we’ll produce a DocuSign SOW within 48 business hours.

I’m available Thu morning for a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
